hints: Remember what actually changes the value of Kc, and what only changes the position of equilibrium without changing Kc.
Kc has jumped from about 0.1 to about 1700, so the equilibrium ratio of products to reactants has become hugely larger.
Link that large shift to the right with the sign of delta H for the forward reaction to decide whether heating or cooling favours products.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two Kc values**

Think of Kc as a measure of how product-rich the equilibrium mixture is. Here it goes up enormously.

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{NO}_2]^2}{[\text{N}_2\text{O}_4]}$$

Going from $1.15 \times 10^{-1}$ to $1.70 \times 10^{3} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ means much more $\text{NO}_2$ relative to $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$, so equilibrium has shifted strongly to the right.

**Recall what can change Kc**

This is the key rule. Changing concentration or pressure shifts the position of equilibrium, but Kc stays the same. Only a change in temperature changes the value of Kc.

**Use delta H to find the temperature change**

The forward reaction is endothermic:

$$\text{N}_2\text{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2 \quad \Delta H = +58.0 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction, which here is forwards. That produces more $\text{NO}_2$ and increases Kc, exactly matching the observation.

options.A: Increasing pressure shifts this equilibrium to the left toward fewer gas moles (1 mole of N2O4 versus 2 moles of NO2), but it does not change Kc. Kc would stay constant, not increase hugely.
options.B: Decreasing pressure would shift the position to the right toward more gas moles, giving more NO2, but the value of Kc would remain unchanged. It cannot explain a change from 0.115 to 1700.
options.C: Only temperature changes Kc. The forward reaction is endothermic (+58.0 kJ mol-1), so higher temperature favours formation of NO2 and gives a much larger Kc. This fits the large increase observed.
options.D: Decreasing temperature favours the exothermic direction, which here is the reverse reaction to form N2O4. That would decrease [NO2] and decrease Kc, the opposite of what is seen.
